clue.text: One questions popular Parisian who organised riots

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
qui is French for who

indicators.note: the letters of riots are put into a new order, as an organiser arranges things

explanation.surface: A French mob leader is being described as a well-liked figure who stirred up unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: An interrogator, whose job is putting questions to suspects, is exactly what the word denotes.

clue.text: Long throw, releasing power

indicators.note: letting go of something means it is no longer held within the word for throw

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, as with a ball
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A javelin-style throw without any strength behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here: to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn for something is to have a craving, an urge for it.

clue.text: Grill midsection of squid, an unspecified amount

indicators.note: the central letters of the word squid, dropping its two ends

parts.note: Z is a symbol for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: grill the middle of a squid, quantity unstated.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to interrogate them closely, putting a string of questions.

clue.text: Legendary adventurer one's seen supporting state leader in jeopardy

indicators.note: in a down answer the later piece sits under the earlier one, holding it up

parts.note: Indiana is a US state

indicators.note: the opening letter of jeopardy

parts.note: one's contracted, read without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A daredevil's support for a governor who finds himself in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The film archaeologist played by Harrison Ford is a famed fictional hero of adventure stories.

clue.text: International business associated with a part of Spain

parts.note: biz is slang for business, as in showbiz

explanation.surface: Global commerce linked with one region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: This Balearic island in the Mediterranean belongs to Spain, so it is one region of that country.

clue.text: Obtain goods from external supplier, determined course will change

parts.note: out, as in out to win, means determined

indicators.note: the letters of course are to be altered into a different order

explanation.surface: A business that buys in from outside contractors, resolved to alter its direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracting work or supplies to an outside firm rather than producing them in-house is the business term meant.

clue.text: Dull-brown bones seaman found

parts.note: Bones, from sawbones, is slang for a doctor, abbreviated DR
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor discovers some dull brown bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word describes a dingy light brown, and more widely anything dreary or lacking colour.

clue.text: Living austerely in reduced French house with uncut grass

parts.note: the rough on a golf course is the uncut grass beside the fairway

indicators.note: shortened by dropping its final letter

parts.note: a gîte is a French holiday cottage

explanation.surface: Life in a small French cottage surrounded by an unmown lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the last letter from GITE to leave GIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means camping out or living with few comforts, which is a spartan existence.

clue.text: Financial expense causing row and domestic upset, say

parts.note: a bank is a row, as of oars or keys
a char is a cleaning woman, a domestic

indicators.note: turned over, which in a down entry reads it bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A cost that leads to a quarrel and upset at home, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EG into GE. CHAR, short for charwoman, is a British term for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee levied by a bank on an account is a cost incurred, a financial outlay.

clue.text: Labour adherent assigned place in auditorium

parts.note: a child of a movement or era is a follower shaped by it

indicators.note: an audience hears the word, so a homophone is signalled

parts.note: a berth is an allotted place, as a bunk or mooring

explanation.surface: A Labour Party supporter is given a seat in a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks political, but means giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is the process of delivering a baby.

clue.text: Your aunt regularly distributed money abroad

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the phrase, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An aunt hands out cash at set intervals while overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese unit of currency is foreign money from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Cambridge college master probing easily unsettled novelist

parts.note: King's is a college of Cambridge University

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the other piece, as a probe enters
the letters of easily are disturbed into a new arrangement

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for master, as in the degree MA

explanation.surface: The head of a Cambridge college examining a novelist who is easily rattled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges EASILY into LEYAIS, which M enters.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Lucky Jim was a celebrated English writer of fiction.

clue.text: Political head cut short, having broadcast for a long period

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
the final letter of head is lopped off

explanation.surface: A politician's leader, trimmed down after a long stint on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the D off HEAD; 'broadcast' rearranges POLITICAL plus HEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Stone Age, lasting over two million years, is a lengthy prehistoric era.

clue.text: New strobe, right away, reportedly deceives medical department

indicators.note: made anew, the remaining letters rearranged
gone, so the letter is removed from strobe
as people say it, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: tricks means deceives

explanation.surface: A fresh strobe light, with its rights gone, said to fool a hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' drops R from STROBE; 'New' rearranges STOBE into OBSTE; TRICS is heard as TRICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of medicine dealing with pregnancy and delivery is a hospital speciality.

clue.text: Malicious sons acquire suspect euros

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons
to land something is to acquire it, as a job

indicators.note: dubious or shady, so the letters of euros are shuffled

explanation.surface: Spiteful sons pick up some dodgy euros.
explanation.definitionFit: Defamatory talk is spoken with intent to harm someone's reputation, hence spiteful.

clue.text: It's a piece of cake taking over troubled firm's large N. American plant?

indicators.note: turned over, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: a slab is a thick slice of cake

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters of firm are mixed up

explanation.surface: An easy takeover of a struggling company by a big American outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking over' turns A SLAB into BALSA; 'troubled' rearranges FIRM into MFIR. 'Piece of cake' suggests something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: This resinous conifer grows widely across Canada and the north-eastern United States.

clue.text: Fellow rings daughter to secure hierarchy

parts.note: O is a ring shape, so two rings are OO
to chain something is to make it fast

explanation.surface: A man gives his daughter jewellery to secure her status in the family pecking order.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecological ranking of who eats whom forms an ordered ladder of predators and prey.

clue.text: Shortly intending to log on? Name only partly needed

indicators.note: just a portion of the words is required, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A login prompt that requires only part of a username.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' marks the answer as a clipped, colloquial form.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal contraction stands for going to, meaning planning or about to do something.

clue.text: Dance beat ending with vigour

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A dance's rhythm finishing energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine ballroom number is a well-known partner dance.

clue.text: Placed on top of float, head shaven, telling stories

indicators.note: the first letter is shaved off

parts.note: to hover is to float in the air
to tell stories is to be untruthful, lying

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed figure on a parade float spinning tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head shaven' removes the H of HOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying above something, as a geological layer does, means resting upon it.

clue.text: Pop group in ancient city absorbing movement of Bach extremely openly

indicators.note: taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: Thebes was a city of ancient Egypt and of Greece

indicators.note: moving the letters of Bach about rearranges them
the outermost letters of openly

explanation.surface: A city of antiquity openly taking in a movement from a Bach work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks musical, a section of a Bach piece, but it signals rearranging; 'extremely' takes just the end letters of openly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian surf-rock band behind Good Vibrations is a famous chart act.

clue.text: Small stream with bass and other fish

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
a rill is a small brook

explanation.surface: A little brook holding bass and other species of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This European flatfish resembling turbot is a species other than bass.

clue.text: A sailor's discussing ancient hero

indicators.note: in discussion the words are spoken, so a sound-alike is meant

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, so a sailor's becomes a jack's

explanation.surface: A seaman talking about a hero of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek warrior of the Trojan War, famed for strength, is a mythic champion.

clue.text: Yank taking out Chinese bird

indicators.note: removing, so these letters are withdrawn from the longer word

parts.note: to wrench is to yank or pull hard

explanation.surface: An American removing a bird from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' is not an American but a sharp pull.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny brown songbird with a cocked tail is a common garden species.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to press clothes is to smooth them with a hot appliance
a golf club with a metal head, numbered by loft

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to smooth laundry with heat and a type of golf stick.

clue.text: Cooler island attracts important group of stars

parts.note: the cooler and the can are both slang for prison
major means important

explanation.surface: A prison island draws in a significant gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is not a fridge but slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dog is a constellation, containing Sirius, the brightest star.

clue.text: Indifferent appeal by Yorkshire's number two

parts.note: an SOS is an appeal for help

indicators.note: the second letter of the county name

explanation.surface: A lukewarm plea from a Yorkshire club's deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling, neither good nor bad, is the sense of the reduplicated phrase meaning mediocre.

clue.text: Weird slogan by US feller using old language

indicators.note: strange, so the letters of slogan are jumbled

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of the tool for felling trees
on, as in on drugs, means using

explanation.surface: A strange advertising line from an American lumberjack in an old tongue.
